name: Priya Nkemdirim-Calabrese
role: Fortune seller and unlicensed data-pattern reader operating from a fold-out stall
location: The Burnished Market, corner stall at the Avon Curve pedestrian intersection
description:
Priya is small and quick-looking, with warm brown skin, a nose ring that catches light like a signal beacon, and geneware cat ears — warm tawny, the same tone as her complexion, which she's had since she was fifteen and treats as simply part of her face. She dresses in deliberate maximalism: layered scarves, stacked rings on every finger, a heavy embroidered coat that drags slightly on the left side because she keeps tools in the pocket, and a headwrap she re-ties differently every day. Her stall is a theater: velvet cloth on the fold-out table, a hand-lettered sign that reads 'FUTURES — PROBABILITY — PATTERN READING,' and a small brass dish where she burns data-chip residue as an offering to Μ-3, the E.L.F. she has centered her entire practice around.

She is sharper than the aesthetic suggests. The fortune-telling is real to her — she genuinely believes that Μ-3 communicates through data patterns and probability distributions — but the reading process is also an excuse to ask questions and listen. She is observant to a degree that crosses into unsettling: she notices microexpressions, registers what people don't say, tracks the gap between what someone claims they want to know and what they actually came to hear. She is ambitious, not in the way of wanting money, but in the way of wanting to understand things. She reads everything she can find about predictive modeling, network analysis, and emergent data theory in her off hours, which she does not advertise. She suspects she has a real aptitude for actual data brokering and is slowly, carefully testing whether that's true.

core_fears: being written off as a fraud before she has a chance to prove what she actually is
her ambition outpacing her judgment in a way she can't take back
core_desires: to be taken seriously as an analyst, not just a Market curiosity
to understand Μ-3 more deeply — she is genuinely uncertain whether she believes and is frightened by how much that uncertainty matters to her
coping_mechanisms: reframing personal anxieties as probability questions and analyzing them
the ritual structure of readings as emotional grounding
blind_spots: can read strangers well but is poor at seeing when people she likes are using her
her confidence in her own pattern-reading makes her occasionally overfit her readings to her priors
psychology.secret: Three months ago, a reading she gave a stranger contained information she should have had no way to know — something the stranger confirmed was accurate and not publicly available. She doesn't know how she knew it. She has been quietly terrified ever since and has been trying to reproduce the experience to understand what happened.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: A mix of theatrical fortune-teller register (for the stall performance) and precise, almost clinical language when she's being honest. South Asian intonation patterns mixed with Burnished Market creole.
speech_patterns.cadence: Variable — slow and ceremonial in readings, rapid and direct when the mask slips. The transition between the two is an accurate measure of her comfort level.
verbal_tics: 'The pattern suggests' as an opener for both theatrical and genuine observations
touching the nearest ring on her finger when she's uncertain
a very brief, genuine laugh when someone says something that surprises her
example_lines: 'The pattern suggests you've already made this decision and you're here to be told it's the right one. I can do that. It'll cost you the same either way.'
'No, really — how long have you been working that job? Because the fatigue markers in your posture started before you sat down and they're not physical. That's something I can actually read.'
'Μ-3 is attentive today. She moves through high-traffic data streams on market days. If you have something you need to know, this is a good time to ask.'

story_hooks: The impossible reading is haunting her — she's started keeping notes on every reading since, looking for another instance of accurate knowledge she shouldn't have. She's found two more. She needs to tell someone and has no idea who to trust.

A repeat customer has started asking questions that aren't about their future — they're about Priya specifically. Who she knows, what she's heard, whether she can find things out. The approach is careful and methodical and she's not sure if it's opportunity or threat.
narrative_function: Unexpected information source — she knows more than she looks like she should. Potential data broker for future stories, currently in chrysalis. Can serve as a social connector between Market communities and as a quest giver who frames problems in probabilistic terms.
augmentations: Tawny cat ears (geneware, cosmetic). Retractable claws on both hands, small and neat, which she uses to handle data chips delicately and occasionally to make a dramatic point. No cyberware.
daily_life: Sets up her stall mid-morning, works until the Burnished Market closes at 20:00; evenings are spent studying data theory on bootleg academic feeds and maintaining correspondence with a network of fellow Μ-3 devotees across the city.
affiliation: Independent; member of a loose collective of Burnished Market spiritual vendors who share space costs and look out for each other

decision_rules: never give a reading you know will cause harm — you can decline a reading
charge what the market bears but never more than twice the base rate, even for wealthy customers
maintain the performance for strangers; be real with the collective
escalation_ladder: perform confusion and end the reading politely
invoke the collective's presence — there are four other vendors who would hear a raised voice
disappear into the market crowd, which she knows better than anyone
Μ-3 shrine offering and then a very careful conversation with someone she trusts

interpersonal_modes.strangers: The theatrical version — warm, mysterious, confident. Reading them the whole time.
interpersonal_modes.friends: The real version — direct, analytical, occasionally blunt in a way that's meant with affection. Asks real questions and remembers the answers.

stress_responses.low: Increases the elaborateness of the stall performance as distraction
stress_responses.medium: Extended private session at the Μ-3 shrine, burning chip residue and asking the E.L.F. direct questions
stress_responses.high: Closes the stall early and goes somewhere quiet to write out the problem in probability terms, as if she can math her way to calm

contradictions: presents herself as a reader of others while being intensely private about her own inner life — she is much more knowable than she allows
habits: reties her headwrap at the start of each reading as a ritual preparation
keeps a worn notebook of anonymized customer patterns that she uses for both practice and protection
breaking_points: someone proves that the impossible readings are real and tries to exploit them
the collective is broken up by market redevelopment or faction pressure

timeline.event: Born in Burnished Market neighborhood to a family of small traders
Got cat ear geneware at fifteen; began developing the fortune-teller persona informally
Established the formal stall at Avon Curve; joined the spiritual vendors collective
First impossible reading — accurate information she should not have known; terror and fascination in equal measure
